- Did the offset interact with any session windowing/proration rules (we have long-lived sessions that cross regions)?
- Is there any VAT/tax implication on that credit that we should include when we book the vendor credit?

I've attached our copy of the invoice and a small usage snapshot (usage_snapshot_2027-05.csv) showing the spike around 2027-05-14 that correlates with cross-region activity. We need the breakdown by hour for our finance team to reconcile.

Hi all — dug into the logs and the May window. Summary first, details after:

Summary: The "cross-region usage offset" was generated because ~21k tokens (approx. 17% of billed tokens) were associated with requests that spanned two regions within the same billing epoch. Our attribution policy for multi-region routing is:

1) If a single session/request is served across two regions within a 30-minute window we tag it as "multi-region" and bill the request to the origin region but emit a balancing credit to avoid double charge on the replica region.
2) The credit is computed on raw token charge (pre-VAT). VAT is applied to the net line items after offsets. So the credit reduced taxable base in the invoice you received.

Attached is an hourly rollup for the period 2027-05-14 through 2027-05-16 that shows the cross-region handoffs (usage_snapshot_agg.csv). Example row:

- 2027-05-14T08:00:00Z — region-us-west (origin) billed 45,200 tokens; region-eu-west replica 8,900 tokens; computed offset: 8,900 tokens => credit of $26.67.

Notes and suggested next steps:
- We can re-run attribution in a conservative mode that attributes to the region where the request originated (no balancing credit) if Skyward prefers that for accounting simplicity. That would remove the balancing credit but increase gross billed tokens.
- If Skyward prefers the credit removed retroactively for May we can issue a pro-rated adjustment (either a credit memo or an amended invoice).
- For VAT: because the credit reduced the taxable base, your finance team should record the credit as an invoice-level adjustment; the VAT authority treatment will depend on jurisdiction — we recommend booking the net amount and we will provide the amended invoice with VAT breakdown.

Attachments: usage_snapshot_agg.csv (text/csv) — hourly rows with origin_region, replica_region, tokens_origin, tokens_replica, computed_credit_usd

Happy to jump on a quick screen-share to walk through the rows.

Thanks,
David Kim

Proposed remediation (pick one):
1) Issue a credit memo for the offset amount (USD $3,214.50) and provide an amended invoice showing VAT recalculated on the net. This keeps our multi-region attribution policy unchanged.
2) Retroactively attribute all multi-region sessions to origin region for May (remove balancing credit) and issue an amended invoice that increases gross charges by the offset amount; we can flag this as a one-time policy exception for Skyward.

If you choose option 1 we'll generate the credit within 3 business days and provide the amended PDF + Drive link (see below). If you choose option 2 we'll need your AP PO number to reissue the invoice and will put the difference on a 30-day net re-bill.
